lesson.text: Electric and magnetic forces act at a distance, through fields you can't see: a magnet pulls a paper clip without touching it.
Like charges or poles repel; opposite ones attract. North pushes north away but pulls south.
Electric forces get stronger with more charge and when objects are closer. Magnetic forces get stronger with stronger magnets and when closer.
An electromagnet is a coil of wire with current flowing through it. More coils, more current, or an iron core make it stronger.

exercises.prompt: What happens when two north poles are brought together?
A magnet can pull a paper clip without touching it.
What happens with a north pole and a south pole?

choices: a coil of wire with current flowing through it
exercises.explain: Current in a coil makes a magnet.

exercises.prompt: Magnetic forces get stronger when the magnets are closer.
How can you make an electromagnet stronger?
A balloon rubbed on hair sticks to a wall. What force is this?
exercises.explain: The balloon has an electric charge.

exercises.prompt: Why is an electromagnet useful in a scrapyard crane?
choices: It can be switched off to drop the metal.
exercises.explain: Switching off the current drops the load.

exercises.prompt: Two objects with the same electric charge attract each other.
Which core makes an electromagnet strongest?
Two charged balloons repel. What happens to the force as they move farther apart?
An electromagnet picks up 5 clips with 10 coils. About how many with 20 coils (same current)?
How can iron filings show a magnet's field?
choices: They line up along the field lines.
exercises.explain: They line up along the invisible field.

exercises.prompt: Electric and magnetic forces can act without touching.
exercises.explain: Yes: they act at a distance.

exercises.prompt: Order from weakest electromagnet to strongest.
exercises.hint: Coils and a core add strength.
exercises.explain: More coils, then an iron core, make it stronger.
